A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STP study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Renamed model variants and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Lean and Isabelle training experiments, benchmark evaluations, and ablations in Sections 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 reports original training and benchmark results, retains ablations, and adds a manual analysis of unproved LeanWorkbook statements in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a Lean verification-time penalty, beta^T, to proof weighting. Appendix A.5 and Algorithm 4 change conjecture reweighting from one nearest match per statement to multiple matches determined by a statement-specific weight. These refine the existing STP procedure; its architecture and three training stages remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use LeanWorkbook, its Isabelle translation, the same proof libraries, miniF2F, ProofNet, and PutnamBench. The validation datasets already participate in v1's extended training experiment. The new audit examines existing LeanWorkbook coverage rather than adding a domain or test environment.

E2.justification: Table 3 drops the separate LeanWorkbook-only STP comparison variant: v1 reports both STP training variants, whereas v4 reports only the revised full model. The external competitors in Tables 1 and 3, and the expert-iteration and parallel-sampling comparisons, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v1 reports 24 Lean training iterations, followed by eight additional iterations incorporating validation statements for its extended variant. v4's main experiment uses all three datasets for 48 iterations, with validation-statement matching weights increased after iteration 24. The reported token budget changes from 19.8B to 51.3B. PutnamBench's smaller sampling budget changes from 64 to 128, and the new audit introduces random selection and manual assessment of 20 unproved statements.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a targeted error analysis assessing formalization accuracy and mathematical correctness for 20 unproved LeanWorkbook statements. The existing training-signal analysis, expert-iteration comparison, and with/without-conjectures retraining ablation remain; Table 2 updates the latter for the revised model.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 newly reports a 95% confidence interval of 38.7%–68.5% for the estimated achievable LeanWorkbook pass rate, based on the audit. Existing benchmark uncertainty reporting remains, without a newly stated repeated-run or seed protocol.

E6.justification: The revised training run reports 28.5% on LeanWorkbook versus v1's 26.3%. Table 1 replaces the validation-augmented model's 61.7%/23.1% miniF2F/ProofNet results at pass@3200 with 65.0%/23.9%, while retaining the original LeanWorkbook-only results under a new label. Table 2's retraining advantage becomes 2.9/2.1 percentage points instead of 1.1/1.1. Table 3 reports 8/644 at 3200 samples instead of the earlier augmented model's 9/644. These are results under revised training conditions. The audit additionally reports 16 correctly formalized and seven provable statements out of 20.

T1.justification: The Wasserstein derivation, Equations 1–16, and theoretical Algorithm 3 remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds explicit mathematical counterexamples to invalid dataset statements, including the assignments in rows 3 and 12. These constitute limited additions of mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims that coupled conjecturing and proving supplies training signals beyond fixed statements, scales better than expert iteration, and achieves leading whole-proof benchmark performance. Updated numerical evidence does not redefine these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: v4 newly qualifies LeanWorkbook performance by explaining that many remaining statements are unprovable, including because of missing assumptions, and estimating a dataset-imposed ceiling. It also explicitly interprets the retained LeanWorkbook-only experiment as evidence of generalization, while acknowledging the base model's prior exposure to validation statements.

D1.justification: v4 newly announces and links a release of the code, model, and dataset. It supplies the verification-time discount, the matching-weight schedule, and PutnamBench commit d49896f, and restores missing content in the Lean proof example in Appendix A.1. These materially expand reproducibility information; the linked resources were not accessed.

R1.justification: v4 adds Yang et al.'s Formal Mathematical Reasoning: A New Frontier in AI and Sun et al.'s Dual Policy Iteration to the references. Section 2 stops describing Poesia et al. as concurrent, while retaining the substantive comparison with that work and the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from Beyond Limited Data to STP, terminology and citation phrasing receive local edits, and Section 4.2 is revised around the longer experiment and dataset audit. Appendix B.3 is added, but the overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–5 receive axis, title, or legend revisions, with Figures 2–3 displaying updated results. Table 1 relabels STP variants, Table 3 is shortened and relocated, and Appendix B.3 adds a multipage audit table. Truncated Lean code displays are repaired within the existing visual design.

improvement.justification: The new LeanWorkbook audit gives the low training pass rate a concrete data-quality qualification, while corrected proof examples, additional settings, a benchmark revision identifier, and resource-access information improve assessability and reproducibility. The longer Lean experiment strengthens scaling evidence, but changed training conditions prevent attributing higher scores to individual refinements, and the reported PutnamBench best result decreases from nine to eight. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
